correctness.rationale: The greedy-arch lemma is proved with an explicit absent target; the finite-state transitions exhaust all words avoiding 000 and 111, including the empty word and run-two boundary. Algebra yields the rational generating function and all k coefficients exactly. The analytic simple dominant positive root, its root derivatives and the local quasi-power expansion rigorously imply mean, variance and CLT. The accompanying checker independently computes brute histograms, formal coefficient distribution, automaton recurrence and direct subsequence universality for all admissible words up to the stated finite cutoffs; replay returned VERIFY_OK. No finite data are presented as a proof of the asymptotic.

originality.rationale: Exact equality was checked against the three-state formal-language derivation and full primary statements. The 2023 regular-language counting theorem can calculate individual restricted counts from a DFA, but neither states the three-state rational law nor the explicit golden-ratio mean/variance and Gaussian limit for the homogeneous-run-two source. The full published unrestricted binary formula counts a different sample space and cannot be specialized by mere parameter relabeling. A full-text comparison found no result directly covering this concrete all-length theorem; unindexed special cases remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently phrased specialized forbidden-run subsequence-universality formulas could antedate this calculation.
General regular-language counting is already known and may yield the finite counts when instantiated; novelty asserted only for the concrete explicit closed form and statistical asymptotic law.
No independent full-literature priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The language forbidding 000 and 111 is the canonical run-length-two binary constrained source. Unlike generic counting decidability, the precise distribution and the mean-rate shift from n/3 to n/sqrt(5), paired with the sharply reduced nonzero variance and central-limit theorem, quantify the universality information carried by this natural source at all lengths. These are motivated structural probabilistic invariants, not arbitrary small finite slice values.
